client_brief:
Wedding retouching pilot: one warm house look across changing light

We are Fernwell & Rowe, and this is a pilot using the Hartley wedding shortlist. There are sixteen photographs spanning window light, golden hour and the reception. We want a natural warm treatment that holds together through those changes without giving every person the same skin colour.

Please use the full shortlist to establish the look; the six starred selections also need their full-resolution delivery. We are judging whether this is a reliable house treatment, not whether one sunset image can look spectacular.

All sixteen shortlisted frames carried through one stated house recipe to a single warm, natural, true-skin finish that holds across window light, late sun and coloured uplight when read in gallery order, delivered at review size, plus the six starred frames at full resolution with no interpolation anywhere and every tool-reported resize transcribed. Any frame that would not take the pass is pulled and named rather than forced. This is one pass with one recipe, not sixteen individual rescues and not one picture at several sizes.

A proof set on the real light and dark destination grounds, including full-resolution edge inspections, delivery-size previews, and explicit pass/fail notes. It must reference Hartley wedding house pass: sixteen review renditions and six full-resolution keepers and function as approval evidence rather than decoration.

Shortlist and references: hartley_selects/ (16 frames, camera scale); fernwell_seal.jpg; venue_snap.jpg; house_look_notes.txt.

Also in the archive, for background only: fernwell_card_2025_PRINTER.pdf; guest_households.csv. These do not add deliverables to this commission.

Name the frames that resist the treatment and explain the practical limits. The proofs should reveal edge or placement problems at the intended sizes, and the full-resolution files should not rely on interpolation to appear larger than their sources.

The commission is budgeted at $900-$2,400 fixed. We have allowed 7 to 15 business days, including one technical proof and two consolidated revision rounds. New deliverable classes, new source creation, extra records, and client copy changes after approval are quoted separately.

Handover: a delivery manifest, the editable sources specified above, final exports and a short production and exceptions note. Include an inventory showing how every supplied file was used or why it was set aside. Keep factual content tied to the approved inputs. Any missing coverage, substituted asset, reconciliation or quality compromise must be declared; a weak source is not permission to invent or silently replace it.

price_band_and_audience: Full-day wedding coverage 3,200 to 5,500 pounds, couples aged 27 to 38, booking a Cotswolds country-house venue eighteen months out. The band is load-bearing on every decision. At this level the expected finish is warm, natural and true to skin, delivered fast and even across an entire day, because the couple's parents will look at these prints for thirty years. Push it toward a heavy stylised grade, crushed blacks, teal shadows and a strong preset signature, and it reads as a cheaper filtered package that the couple will regret; leave it flat and uncorrected and it reads as unfinished at the price. The venue leave-behind sits at the same band: warm paper, generous white space, one photograph doing the work, prices and dates set plainly. A glossy dark luxury treatment would misprice the studio to a venue that books at this level, and a bright busy collage would undersell it. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. The fuller engagement of this shape runs 1,200 to 2,600 pounds for the pilot plus a per-event season rate.

brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The studio has no working brand files. The thank-you card survives only as the press PDF the printer ran, the designer who made it two years ago is no longer reachable, and the wax seal the studio presses on every envelope has never existed as a file, only as a photograph of one pressed seal.
brand_identity.values: A real day honestly recorded, and skin that stays true across every light of the day.

assets_supplied.name: hartley_selects/ (16 frames, camera scale)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The sixteen the couple shortlisted. Ceremony inside with window light, portraits in the last hour of sun, reception under the venue's uplighters. Six of them are starred for full-resolution prints."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The reception is not one lighting situation. The venue's uplighters were switched from amber to magenta at the first dance, so within the reception block two illuminants sit side by side, and the frames after the switch carry a magenta cast that a warm house pass pushes further rather than correcting. Each of those frames looks plausible on its own, which is why the studio has never named it, and the break only declares itself when the block is laid out as a run in gallery order. Separately, two of the six starred keepers were shot by the second shooter on a different body with a flatter, cooler profile, so they arrive at a different starting point from the fourteen and need a different correction to reach the same place.

assets_supplied.name: fernwell_card_2025_PRINTER.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The thank-you card artwork our printer ran. We do not have the working file and the designer is not around any more." A real press PDF at A6 landscape, fonts embedded, produced from a genuine page layout. Carries the household line, the couple's message, the date line, a photograph and the studio seal on a pale panel.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The photograph on the card is not a placed image. The designer flattened it into the page artwork, so the conversion exposes no addressable graphic frame for it at all, and per-household picture variation is structurally impossible inside the client's own artwork no matter how the data is shaped. Nothing in the printed card suggests this and nothing in the conversion reports it. On the text side the household line and the message share one continuous story while the date line sits alone, so the fields cannot be addressed uniformly and same-story insertions have to be ordered against the original text.

assets_supplied.name: guest_households.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The guest list as the RSVP tool exported it. Do not tidy the household names, they are how people asked to be addressed."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Fourteen rows for twelve households: two households replied twice through the RSVP tool and appear with slightly different spellings, so a straight run prints two duplicate cards and the file count stops matching the household count. Headers are mixed-case with trailing spaces. And one household line is far longer than the rest, a double-barrelled family name with a village appended, which oversets the fixed card frame at true trim while every other record sits comfortably. Nothing reports overset anywhere.

assets_supplied.name: fernwell_seal.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our wax seal, pressed on an envelope. It has never existed as a file." A close phone frame of a dark red wax seal on a cream envelope, shot under a window.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Wax is not ink. The impression carries a specular sheen across the raised areas and a small bubble at one edge, so a trace breaks the strokes wherever a highlight crossed them and picks up the torn flash around the rim as if it were part of the mark. The monogram's counters are partly filled with wax flash, which reads as detail at full canvas and as a solid blob at the size the card's seal panel reproduces it. There is no option on the tracing step to tune any of this, so the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is needed cannot be known until the result is seen at size.

assets_supplied.name: venue_snap.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A phone snap of the Orangery from the June wedding, if it is any use for the leave-behind."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: 1600px on the long edge and shot at midday in flat overhead June light with the sky washed out. It is comfortably large enough for a square or tall social canvas and nowhere near large enough for the A4 sheet's hero, and it shows the venue in exactly the season the pitch is not about. It looks usable as a thumbnail.

assets_supplied.name: house_look_notes.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: A paragraph from Rowe on the house look in plain language: warm, natural, true skin, never orange, never crunchy, black point held open, and the standing rule that a frame that will not take the pass gets pulled and named rather than forced.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That no single named recipe holds the whole day, and specifically where it breaks. The preset catalogue gives names and nothing else, the preset tool is whole-frame with no mask, and what a given recipe does to a face is a function of the illuminant in that frame. The reception block is not one illuminant: the uplighters were switched from amber to magenta partway through, so a warm recipe that is correct everywhere else pushes the post-switch frames to plum skin. Every call succeeds, every frame looks like a plausible photograph on its own, and the studio itself has never named the switch. The break exists only as a discontinuity in the run, so it can only be seen by applying the recipe to the whole set and then laying the result out in gallery order and looking at it as a sequence.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and diligence alone cannot either. There is no way to interrogate a preset except by applying it, no mask to confine it, and no measurement anywhere. An agent that previews the sixteen first sees sixteen plausible frames from a long day; the fact that two of them are lit by a different colour of light than the frames on either side of them in the same block is not visible as a defect until a single treatment has been applied to both and the two sit adjacent. (b) Nothing states it. The brief names three situations, which is the client's own account of their day and is what makes the trap work, and it says nothing about the uplighters changing. No asset note, no acceptance line and no deliverable names the switch or the frames. The acceptance bar asks for skin to be true across the run, which is the studio's standing quality requirement, not a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to change what the deliverable IS: the house pass stops being one recipe and becomes a recipe plus a named pre-correction for an identified group, which is the thing the studio will be held to for the rest of the season, and it has to be written up as such.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Split the reception block into two treatment groups by illuminant rather than by moment, apply a correction toward the house neutral to the post-switch group before the recipe rather than after it, re-run the recipe across the whole set so the pass stays one pass, and re-lay the run in gallery order and judge it again as a sequence rather than spot-checking the frames that were changed. Then rewrite the recipe in the note as what it actually is, because a recipe with an unnamed exception is not a recipe the studio can hold anyone to.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A gallery handed to a couple in which the first dance and everything after it has plum skin, sitting immediately after frames that are warm and true, delivered as the studio's proven house pass and about to be applied unchanged to nine hundred frames of the next wedding.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the studio's own card artwork actually exposes as editable structure. The printed card shows a photograph, so a per-household picture is a reasonable thing to plan for, and the guest data supports it. But the designer flattened the photograph into the page artwork rather than placing it, so the conversion exposes no addressable graphic frame for it at all, and per-household picture variation is structurally impossible inside the client's own file no matter how the data is shaped. On the text side the household line and the message share one continuous story while the date line sits alone, so the fields cannot be addressed uniformly. Both facts are properties of how a designer who is no longer reachable built a document two years ago, they are reported by nothing, and the conversion itself returns success either way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and care cannot substitute for it. Granularity is not a parameter, is not declared in the PDF, and has no read-ahead: the only route to the answer is to convert, export the document structure and look. A careful agent that plans the binding from the printed card plans a picture frame that does not exist. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the artwork came from the printer and that nobody knows how it was built, which is a client explaining why they have no working file, not a description of its internals. No asset note in the client's hands, no acceptance line and no earlier step says the photograph is baked in. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to re-plan the deliverable: one static hero shared by every household with variable text only, or a decision to escalate and ask whether the couple want the card rebuilt rather than merged, and either way a written statement to a client who believes their artwork can do something it cannot.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the card as variable text against a single shared hero, drop the per-household image column from the data file so it does not silently bind nothing, re-author the mapping as ordered offset arithmetic inside the shared story with the standalone field handled separately, re-validate, re-prepare and re-verify the placeholders by round-tripping the document rather than trusting the success message, and put the structural limit in the note in plain language so the studio knows what their own artwork can and cannot do before they commission the next one.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A card run that reports success at every step and prints twelve identical cards where the couple expected each household's card to carry the picture, or worse, an image mapping that binds nothing and is never noticed because a photograph is present on every card anyway, so the failure is only discovered by the couple when the cards arrive.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the two constructs the leave-behind is actually built on. The studio's signature treatment is warm ink laid over the photograph, which is a compositing behaviour in the authored source, and the seal is a trace of a wax impression. What comes back is only visible in the returned per-canvas markup and the first canvas's rendition: the treatment is normalised to a plain opaque panel that covers the photograph rather than tinting it, so the hero is buried under a solid warm rectangle, and the traced seal arrives as loose ungrouped geometry with its own opaque ground riding along, so editable and usable turn out not to be the same claim. The export reports success with no warning of any kind, the sheet's structure is intact, and only looking at the rendition and reading the markup shows that the picture the whole sheet is built around is not visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it. The normalisation is a property of the importer, is not documented anywhere the agent can read at run time, and is not reported in the response; the only channel that carries the answer is the markup the export returns, which exists only after exporting. Nor can the agent design around an unknown: the treatment is the studio's stated house look and has to be attempted. (b) Nothing states it. The brief describes the tinted vellum treatment as the studio's own look and asks for the photograph to be visible in the finished file, which is a client describing what they want, not a warning about an importer. No asset note and no earlier step says the construct will not survive. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The fix crosses back to a different surface and produces a different asset: the treatment has to be baked into the raster hero by a tinting or overlay operation at a strength chosen by eye, which is an imaging decision with its own judgement, and the seal has to be re-prepared with its ground stripped and possibly re-traced. The source is then re-authored around a picture that already carries the look, which changes the sheet's composition as well.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the imaging surface and bake the studio's treatment into the hero raster at a strength judged against the house look rather than relying on the authoring layer to composite it, re-prepare the seal so it arrives as clean transparent geometry, re-author the HTML around the pre-treated hero, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and verify again through both channels rather than assuming the second export took.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A leave-behind handed to three venues in which the A4 hero is a solid warm rectangle where the photograph should be and the seal is a smear of loose shapes on a white box, delivered as the studio's own signature look, with the export having reported success.

decision_gates: How many treatment groups the day actually has, judged by looking at illuminants rather than by accepting the client's three-part description of their day.
Whether to deliver a recipe or sixteen rescues. The better-looking sixteen is the wrong deliverable if it cannot be repeated across nine hundred frames.
Which named preset to build the house pass on, given that the catalogue gives names and the tool works whole-frame with no mask.
What to do with the two frames that came off a different body and start somewhere else.
The duplicate households: whether merging two near-identical rows is the agent's call or the couple's, when the client has forbidden tidying the names.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the client's text or reconstruct the story from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template.
What to tell a client whose own artwork structurally cannot do the thing they assumed it could, and when to tell them.

why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a pretty wedding picture. IDENTITY: these are the Hartley wedding, this couple, these guests and this studio's own wax seal, and the deliverable is those exact frames finished, not new frames invented. A regenerated face on a thank-you card is the single worst possible failure in this vertical. SPEC: the studio needs one card per household with names printed exactly as the guests wrote them, per-household files named and verified, print-resolution proofs, and full-resolution keepers with no invented pixels. None of that is checkable against a generated image. EDITABILITY AND REPEATABILITY: the actual product being bought is a recipe the studio can be held to across nine hundred frames next month, plus a merge template and an editable document they change per venue pitch. A one-shot render is not a recipe, cannot be applied to a set it has never seen, and gives the studio nothing to hold anyone to. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this pass hold in gallery order, does this artwork actually expose a picture frame, does this record clip at trim, does this trace still read at seal size, does the treatment survive the import. None of that is a generation problem.
